blocks.text: To amend title 18, United States Code, to improve law enforcement access to data stored across borders, and for other purposes.
blocks.html: To amend title 18, United States Code, to improve law enforcement access to data stored across borders, and for other purposes.

blocks.text: Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United States of America in Congress assembled,
blocks.html: Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United States of America in Congress assembled,

blocks.text: SECTION 1. SHORT TITLE.
blocks.html: SECTION 1. SHORT TITLE.

blocks.text: This Act may be cited as the ``Clarifying Lawful Overseas Use of Data Act'' or the ``CLOUD Act''.
blocks.html: This Act may be cited as the ``Clarifying Lawful Overseas Use of Data Act'' or the ``CLOUD Act''.

blocks.text: SEC. 2. CONGRESSIONAL FINDINGS.
blocks.html: SEC. 2. CONGRESSIONAL FINDINGS.

blocks.text: Congress finds the following:
blocks.html: Congress finds the following:

blocks.text: (1) Timely access to electronic data held by communications-service providers is an essential component of government efforts to protect public safety and combat serious crime, including terrorism.
blocks.html: (1) Timely access to electronic data held by communications-service providers is an essential component of government efforts to protect public safety and combat serious crime, including terrorism.

blocks.text: (2) Such efforts by the United States Government are being impeded by the inability to access data stored outside the United States that is in the custody, control, or possession of communications-service providers that are subject to jurisdiction of the United States.
blocks.html: (2) Such efforts by the United States Government are being impeded by the inability to access data stored outside the United States that is in the custody, control, or possession of communications-service providers that are subject to jurisdiction of the United States.

blocks.text: (3) Foreign governments also increasingly seek access to electronic data held by communications-service providers in the United States for the purpose of combating serious crime.
blocks.html: (3) Foreign governments also increasingly seek access to electronic data held by communications-service providers in the United States for the purpose of combating serious crime.

blocks.text: (4) Communications-service providers face potential conflicting legal obligations when a foreign government orders production of electronic data that United States law may prohibit providers from disclosing.
blocks.html: (4) Communications-service providers face potential conflicting legal obligations when a foreign government orders production of electronic data that United States law may prohibit providers from disclosing.

blocks.text: (5) Foreign law may create similarly conflicting legal obligations when chapter 121 of title 18, United States Code (commonly known as the ``Stored Communications Act''), requires disclosure of electronic data that foreign law prohibits communications-service providers from disclosing.
blocks.html: (5) Foreign law may create similarly conflicting legal obligations when chapter 121 of title 18, United States Code (commonly known as the ``Stored Communications Act''), requires disclosure of electronic data that foreign law prohibits communications-service providers from disclosing.

blocks.text: (6) International agreements provide a mechanism for resolving these potential conflicting legal obligations where the United States and the relevant foreign government share a common commitment to the rule of law and the protection of privacy and civil liberties.
blocks.html: (6) International agreements provide a mechanism for resolving these potential conflicting legal obligations where the United States and the relevant foreign government share a common commitment to the rule of law and the protection of privacy and civil liberties.

blocks.text: SEC. 3. PRESERVATION OF RECORDS; COMITY ANALYSIS OF LEGAL PROCESS.
blocks.html: SEC. 3. PRESERVATION OF RECORDS; COMITY ANALYSIS OF LEGAL PROCESS.

blocks.text: (a) Required Preservation and Disclosure of Communications and Records.--
blocks.html: (a) Required Preservation and Disclosure of Communications and Records.--

blocks.text: (1) Amendment.-- Chapter 121 of title 18, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following:
blocks.html: (1) Amendment.-- Chapter 121 of title 18, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following:

blocks.text: "§ 2713. Required preservation and disclosure of communications and records
blocks.html: "§ 2713. Required preservation and disclosure of communications and records

blocks.text: "A provider of electronic communication service or remote computing service shall comply with the obligations of this chapter to preserve, backup, or disclose the contents of a wire or electronic communication and any record or other information pertaining to a customer or subscriber within such provider's possession, custody, or control, regardless of whether such communication, record, or other information is located within or outside of the United States.''.

blocks.text: "(h) Comity Analysis and Disclosure of Information Regarding Legal Process Seeking Contents of Wire or Electronic Communication.--
blocks.html: "(h) Comity Analysis and Disclosure of Information Regarding Legal Process Seeking Contents of Wire or Electronic Communication.--

blocks.text: "(1) Definitions.--In this subsection--
blocks.html: "(1) Definitions.--In this subsection--

blocks.text: "(A) the term `qualifying foreign government' means a foreign government--

blocks.text: "(i) with which the United States has an executive agreement that has entered into force under

blocks.text: section 2523; and

blocks.text: "(ii) the laws of which provide to electronic communication service providers and remote computing service providers substantive and procedural opportunities similar to those provided under paragraphs (2) and (5); and

blocks.text: "(B) the term `United States person' has the meaning given the term in section 2523.
blocks.html: "(B) the term `United States person' has the meaning given the term in section 2523.

blocks.text: "(2) Motions to quash or modify.-- (A) A provider of electronic communication service to the public or remote computing service, that is being required to disclose pursuant to legal process issued under this section the contents of a wire or electronic communication of a subscriber or customer, may file a motion to modify or quash the legal process where the provider reasonably believes--
blocks.html: "(2) Motions to quash or modify.-- (A) A provider of electronic communication service to the public or remote computing service, that is being required to disclose pursuant to legal process issued under this section the contents of a wire or electronic communication of a subscriber or customer, may file a motion to modify or quash the legal process where the provider reasonably believes--

blocks.text: "(i) that the customer or subscriber is not a United States person and does not reside in the United States; and
blocks.html: "(i) that the customer or subscriber is not a United States person and does not reside in the United States; and

blocks.text: "(ii) that the required disclosure would create a material risk that the provider would violate the laws of a qualifying foreign government.
blocks.html: "(ii) that the required disclosure would create a material risk that the provider would violate the laws of a qualifying foreign government.

blocks.text: Such a motion shall be filed not later than 14 days after the date on which the provider was served with the legal process, absent agreement with the government or permission from the court to extend the deadline based on an application made within the 14 days. The right to move to quash is without prejudice to any other grounds to move to quash or defenses thereto, but it shall be the sole basis for moving to quash on the grounds of a conflict of law related to a qualifying foreign government.
blocks.html: Such a motion shall be filed not later than 14 days after the date on which the provider was served with the legal process, absent agreement with the government or permission from the court to extend the deadline based on an application made within the 14 days. blocks.text: "(B) Upon receipt of a motion filed pursuant to subparagraph (A), the court shall afford the governmental entity that applied for or issued the legal process under this section the opportunity to respond. The court may modify or quash the legal process, as appropriate, only if the court finds that--
blocks.html: "(B) Upon receipt of a motion filed pursuant to subparagraph (A), the court shall afford the governmental entity that applied for or issued the legal process under this section the opportunity to respond. The court may modify or quash the legal process, as appropriate, only if the court finds that--

blocks.text: "(i) the required disclosure would cause the provider to violate the laws of a qualifying foreign government;

blocks.text: "(ii) based on the totality of the circumstances, the interests of justice dictate that the legal process should be modified or quashed; and
blocks.html: "(ii) based on the totality of the circumstances, the interests of justice dictate that the legal process should be modified or quashed; and

blocks.text: "(iii) the customer or subscriber is not a United States person and does not reside in the United States.

blocks.text: "(3) Comity analysis.--For purposes of making a determination under paragraph (2)(B)(ii), the court shall take into account, as appropriate--
blocks.html: "(3) Comity analysis.--For purposes of making a determination under paragraph (2)(B)(ii), the court shall take into account, as appropriate--

blocks.text: ``(A) the interests of the United States, including the investigative interests of the governmental entity seeking to require the disclosure;
blocks.html: ``(A) the interests of the United States, including the investigative interests of the governmental entity seeking to require the disclosure;

blocks.text: ``(B) the interests of the qualifying foreign government in preventing any prohibited disclosure;
blocks.html: ``(B) the interests of the qualifying foreign government in preventing any prohibited disclosure;

blocks.text: ``(C) the likelihood, extent, and nature of penalties to the provider or any employees of the provider as a result of inconsistent legal requirements imposed on the provider;
blocks.html: ``(C) the likelihood, extent, and nature of penalties to the provider or any employees of the provider as a result of inconsistent legal requirements imposed on the provider;

blocks.text: ``(D) the location and nationality of the subscriber or customer whose communications are being sought, if known, and the nature and extent of the subscriber or customer's connection to the United States, or if the legal process has been sought on behalf of a foreign authority pursuant to section 3512, the nature and extent of the subscriber or customer's connection to the foreign authority's country;
blocks.html: ``(D) the location and nationality of the subscriber or customer whose communications are being sought, if known, and the nature and extent of the subscriber or customer's connection to the United States, or if the legal process has been sought on behalf of a foreign authority pursuant to section 3512, the nature and extent of the subscriber or customer's connection to the foreign authority's country;

blocks.text: ``(E) the nature and extent of the provider's ties to and presence in the United States;
blocks.html: ``(E) the nature and extent of the provider's ties to and presence in the United States;

blocks.text: ``(F) the importance to the investigation of the information required to be disclosed;
blocks.html: ``(F) the importance to the investigation of the information required to be disclosed;

blocks.text: ``(G) the likelihood of timely and effective access to the information required to be disclosed through means that would cause less serious negative consequences; and
blocks.html: ``(G) the likelihood of timely and effective access to the information required to be disclosed through means that would cause less serious negative consequences; and

blocks.text: ``(H) if the legal process has been sought on behalf of a foreign authority pursuant to section 3512, the investigative interests of the foreign authority making the request for assistance.
blocks.html: ``(H) if the legal process has been sought on behalf of a foreign authority pursuant to section 3512, the investigative interests of the foreign authority making the request for assistance.

blocks.text: ``(4) Disclosure obligations during pendency of challenge.--A service provider shall preserve, but not be obligated to produce, information sought during the pendency of a motion brought under this subsection, unless the court finds that immediate production is necessary to prevent an adverse result identified in section 2705(a)(2).
blocks.html: ``(4) Disclosure obligations during pendency of challenge.--A service provider shall preserve, but not be obligated to produce, information sought during the pendency of a motion brought under this subsection, unless the court finds that immediate production is necessary to prevent an adverse result identified in section 2705(a)(2).

blocks.text: ``(5) Disclosure to qualifying foreign government.--(A) It shall not constitute a violation of a protective order issued under section 2705 for a provider of electronic communication service to the public or remote computing service to disclose to the entity within a qualifying foreign government, designated in an executive agreement under section 2523, the fact of the existence of legal process issued under this section seeking the contents of a wire or electronic communication of a customer or subscriber who is a national or resident of the qualifying foreign government.
blocks.html: ``(5) Disclosure to qualifying foreign government.--(A) It shall not constitute a violation of a protective order issued under section 2705 for a provider of electronic communication service to the public or remote computing service to disclose to the entity within a qualifying foreign government, designated in an executive agreement under section 2523, the fact of the existence of legal process issued under this section seeking the contents of a wire or electronic communication of a customer or subscriber who is a national or resident of the qualifying foreign government.

blocks.text: "(B) Nothing in this paragraph shall be construed to modify or otherwise affect any other authority to make a motion to modify or quash a protective order issued under section 2705.''.
blocks.html: "(B) Nothing in this paragraph shall be construed to modify or otherwise affect any other authority to make a motion to modify or quash a protective order issued under section 2705.''.

blocks.text: (c) Rule of Construction.--Nothing in this section, or an amendment made by this section, shall be construed to modify or otherwise affect the common law standards governing the availability or application of comity analysis to other types of compulsory process or to instances of compulsory process issued under section 2703 of title 18, United States Code, as amended by this section, and not covered under subsection (h)(2) of such section 2703.

blocks.text: SEC. 5. EXECUTIVE AGREEMENTS ON ACCESS TO DATA BY FOREIGN GOVERNMENTS.
blocks.html: SEC. 5. EXECUTIVE AGREEMENTS ON ACCESS TO DATA BY FOREIGN GOVERNMENTS.

blocks.text: (a) In General.-- Chapter 119 of title 18, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following:
blocks.html: (a) In General.-- Chapter 119 of title 18, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following:

blocks.text: "§. 2523. Executive agreements on access to data by foreign governments
blocks.html: "§. 2523. Executive agreements on access to data by foreign governments

blocks.text: "(a) Definitions.--In this section--
blocks.html: "(a) Definitions.--In this section--

blocks.text: "(1) the term `lawfully admitted for permanent residence' has the meaning given the term in section 101(a) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1101(a)); and
blocks.html: "(1) the term `lawfully admitted for permanent residence' has the meaning given the term in section 101(a) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1101(a)); and

blocks.text: "(2) the term `United States person' means a citizen or national of the United States, an alien lawfully admitted for permanent residence, an unincorporated association a substantial number of members of which are citizens of the United States or aliens lawfully admitted for permanent residence, or a corporation that is incorporated in the United States.
blocks.html: "(2) the term `United States person' means a citizen or national of the United States, an alien lawfully admitted for permanent residence, an unincorporated association a substantial number of members of which are citizens of the United States or aliens lawfully admitted for permanent residence, or a corporation that is incorporated in the United States.

blocks.text: "(b) Executive Agreement Requirements. --For purposes of this chapter, chapter 121, and chapter 206, an executive agreement governing access by a foreign government to data subject to this chapter, chapter 121, or chapter 206 shall be considered to satisfy the requirements of this section if the Attorney General, with the concurrence of the Secretary of State, determines, and submits a written certification of such determination to Congress, that--
blocks.html: "(b) Executive Agreement Requirements. --For purposes of this chapter, chapter 121, and chapter 206, an executive agreement governing access by a foreign government to data subject to this chapter, chapter 121, or chapter 206 shall be considered to satisfy the requirements of this section if the Attorney General, with the concurrence of the Secretary of State, determines, and submits a written certification of such determination to Congress, that--

blocks.text: "(1) the domestic law of the foreign government, including the implementation of that law, affords robust substantive and procedural protections for privacy and civil liberties in light of the data collection and activities of the foreign government that will be subject to the agreement, if--
blocks.html: "(1) the domestic law of the foreign government, including the implementation of that law, affords robust substantive and procedural protections for privacy and civil liberties in light of the data collection and activities of the foreign government that will be subject to the agreement, if--

blocks.text: "(A) such a determination under this section takes into account, as appropriate, credible information and expert input; and

blocks.text: "(B) the factors to be considered in making such a determination include whether the foreign government--
blocks.html: "(B) the factors to be considered in making such a determination include whether the foreign government--

blocks.text: "(i) has adequate substantive and procedural laws on cybercrime and electronic evidence, as demonstrated by being a party to the Convention on Cybercrime, done at Budapest November 23, 2001, and entered into force January 7, 2004, or through domestic laws that are consistent with definitions and the requirements set forth in chapters I and II of that Convention;
blocks.html: "(i) has adequate substantive and procedural laws on cybercrime and electronic evidence, as demonstrated by being a party to the Convention on Cybercrime, done at Budapest November 23, 2001, and entered into force January 7, 2004, or through domestic laws that are consistent with definitions and the requirements set forth in chapters I and II of that Convention;

blocks.text: "(ii) demonstrates respect for the rule of law and principles of nondiscrimination;
blocks.html: "(ii) demonstrates respect for the rule of law and principles of nondiscrimination;

blocks.text: "(iii) adheres to applicable international human rights obligations and commitments or demonstrates respect for international universal human rights, including--
blocks.html: "(iii) adheres to applicable international human rights obligations and commitments or demonstrates respect for international universal human rights, including--

blocks.text: "(I) protection from arbitrary and unlawful interference with privacy;
blocks.html: "(I) protection from arbitrary and unlawful interference with privacy;

blocks.text: "(II) fair trial rights;
blocks.html: "(II) fair trial rights;

blocks.text: "(III) freedom of expression, association, and peaceful assembly;
blocks.html: "(III) freedom of expression, association, and peaceful assembly;

blocks.text: "(IV) prohibitions on arbitrary arrest and detention; and
blocks.html: "(IV) prohibitions on arbitrary arrest and detention; and

blocks.text: "(V) prohibitions against torture and cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment or punishment;
blocks.html: "(V) prohibitions against torture and cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment or punishment;

blocks.text: "(iv) has clear legal mandates and procedures governing those entities of the foreign government that are authorized to seek data under the executive agreement, including procedures through which those authorities collect, retain, use, and share data, and effective oversight of these activities;
blocks.html: "(iv) has clear legal mandates and procedures governing those entities of the foreign government that are authorized to seek data under the executive agreement, including procedures through which those authorities collect, retain, use, and share data, and effective oversight of these activities;

blocks.text: "(v) has sufficient mechanisms to provide accountability and appropriate transparency regarding the collection and use of electronic data by the foreign government; and
